subject: Money
title: Loss Aversion and Money
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Loss Aversion and Money.

hook.text: Losing $100 feels twice as bad as gaining $100 feels good. We're wired to hate losses.

buildup.text: Kahneman and Tversky proved this in 1979. Humans weight losses roughly 2x more than equal gains.

discovery.text: This explains why people hold losing stocks too long. Selling means admitting the loss is real.

twist.text: Marketers exploit this with 'limited time' offers. The fear of missing a deal overrides rational thought.

climax.text: Loss aversion makes us spend to avoid loss and hold to avoid regret. Both cost us money.

punchline.text: Fear of losing beats the joy of gaining.

quiz.question: How much more do we weigh losses compared to gains?
